Sentence (English): GE brand dishwasher, purchased at Home Depot in Derby, CT on 1/1/25, delivered on 1/7/25.
Comments (English): [ Stay away from GE/ Bodewell ] || ---------------- || GE brand dishwasher, purchased at Home Depot in Derby, CT on 1/1/25, delivered on 1/7/25. Selected for: American made, metal tub, steam function and within our budget. Used the dishwasher ~5 times a week.Wed11/5. Loaded the dishwasher before bed, added the cascade packet (recommended by GE), set normal cycle and went to bed.Thr 11/6- washer reading “FTD” error code, the dishes unwashed and the tub of the washer full of dirty food water. Attempted to restart and the error code reappeared.11/6- 1st call to Bodewell to see if the dishwasher was able to be fixed. CSR was dismissive and uninformative. She informed me that a technician would be at my house on F 11/21. I was confused as we had not discussed anything and I asked the CSR to give me a quote for this repair. She responded with “It's under warrantee… everyone knows that.” At no point had she discussed my warrantee nor the steps to proceed. I informed her that she had not communicated with me properly and she dismissed that concern as well. I confirmed (on a recorded line) that the technician would be at my home on 11/21 and that the repairs were 100% covered. She begrudgingly confirmed and we ended the call.On Thr 11/20, I received a call from Bodewell informing me that they were cancelling my Friday 11/21 appointment and rescheduling because I “did not have the necessary parts”. I was then informed that someone had gone in the system, ordered parts to be delivered to my house and that FEDEX had not reported movement on the shipment since 11/18, when they had been mis-shipped to Oregon. I had no idea about this part order, had no tracking information, and the initial CSR had not told me that the tech could not come out without parts. When I asked if anyone had spoken with FEDEX I was told that “was not their job” by Bodewell. I contacted FEDEX myself, filed a claim regarding the missing packages and gave them MY contact information. Bodewell refused to send the technician on 11/21 without those parts being present. I contacted FEDEX on 11/21 and they informed me that there was no movement on the packages and that they were not locatable. I called Bodewell back and informed them of this and the CSR “reordered” the parts to my house with overnight shipping. She then informed me that some of the parts were backordered but she would try to expedite them. My service appointment was rescheduled for Fri 11/28, the day AFTER thanksgiving between 8 and noon.On M 11/24, 3 packages from GE were on my doorstep.F 11/28, A Bodewell technician arrived within the time frame and got to work. GE had sent refrigerator parts to my home. Luckily the third package had a drain pump. The technician performed a general maintenance, changed the drain pump, ran a rinse cycle, deemed the dishwasher all set and left.Two hours later, I loaded the dishwasher, went to run a normal cycle and received FTD error code again. On Friday 11/28, called Bodewell at 4:30 pm to report dishwasher still broken. I was told that a technician would not be able to come out until Fri 12/12- I refused this and asked to be escalated. A supervisor never came on the line, but told the CSR to schedule us with a third-party appliance technician. The CSR scheduled the technician to come out today, Tue 12/2 between 8 and noon.This morning 12/2 I had yet to receive a confirmation. At 11 am I called Bodewell and the CSR gave me the contact information for the appliance repair company. This company is located in BROOKLYN, NY. A TWO HOUR DRIVE from my house. I call the appliance company- they had not received the claim from Bodewell until 9 am this morning 12/2, and could not (understandably) get a technician out to my location today. She asked if she could schedule me for the soonest I was available, which is Thursday 12/4, during the morning.I called Bodewell back to inquire why the CSR that made the appointment on Friday 11/28 had not confirmed with appointment with the company. The CSR's that I spoke to explained that their system does not always send the claim immediately. I explained to the CSR that this was unacceptable, I now had to wait until Thursday, and I asked if on Thursday, if the technician determined that the dishwasher was broken, would they be able to replace the unit. The CSR explained to me that this Thursday would be a diagnostic appointment. And that she was unable to send parts to my home in order to prepare for this maintenance. I asked to be transferred to customer relations.Once on the phone with customer relations, it took 56 minutes for someone to allow me to speak with a supervisor. I spent the entire time attempting to explain that if the procedures had been followed properly, I would already have had a repaired dishwasher, or a replacement on the way. The CSR at customer relations repeated the same line of 'this is how the warranty works' over and over. It seems to me that after one technician had already been out, there should have been some sort of reconciliation made. I asked that this CSR's contact the appliance company in Brooklyn, and ask which parts they thought may be needed to make the repairs on Thursday. At first she refused to make the call, but then she called the company repeatedly and they did not answer. She then informed me that they would not be ordering parts and should not order parts prior to a technician diagnosing the unit. I pointed out that GE had previously ordered parts to my home twice. I finally informed her that I would not be getting off the phone until I spoke with a supervisor.Once I was finally on the phone with a supervisor, the supervisor informed me with 0 hesitation that there was nothing that they would be doing for me that I had to wait for Thursday's appointment- at which point the dishwasher will be diagnosed. On Thursday, Bodewell will once again order parts, I will then have to wait for those parts to come in, and then wait for another appointment for another technician to come and install those parts. If those parts fail, I am still not eligible for a replacement. The supervisor informed me that GE requires the repair of a dishwasher to fail four times before they will issue a replacement.The supervisor noted that I had been lied to multiple times- starting with the fact that I had been informed that a technician could not come to my house without parts already on site. Two separate CSR's had informed me that my maintenance could not happen without those preordered parts. The supervisor seemed to think that I had originally had a technician out for a diagnostic appointment when I had never previously spoken to a technician before 11/28. The supervisor informed me that they are not allowed to order parts prior to a diagnostic appointment. This has occurred twice since my dishwasher broke.So- I am now set with a dilemma, I have a technician coming on Thursday who is unprepared (to no fault of their own) to fix my dishwasher. The GE/ Bodewell Warranty is nothing more than a con in order to make sales.It is costing both Bodewell and myself more money than it would cost for them to just replace the dishwasher.I will never buy another GE appliance again, and I encourage all my friends and family to follow suit. If you happen to have a GE appliance, pay close attention to the fact that your warranty does not actually cover the replacement of your appliance unless it has been repaired multiple times. You will wait months for these repairs, during which time your family will have to go through the same things that I go through. I am spending more time hand-washing dishes, and arguing with CSR's on the phone, than I am spending time with my family during the holiday season. I find GE, and their appliance repair company Bodewell, to be extremely negligent, rude, and ineffective.

Two separate CSR's had informed me that my maintenance could not happen without those preordered parts. The supervisor informed me that they are not allowed to order parts prior to a diagnostic appointment. You will wait months for these repairs, during which time your family will have to go through the same things that I go through. I am spending more time hand-washing dishes, and arguing with CSR's on the phone, than I am spending time with my family during the holiday season. I find GE, and their appliance repair company Bodewell, to be extremely negligent, rude, and ineffective.

Comments (English): [ Quiet and efficient ] || ---------------- || I got this dishwasher to replace one from another brand that gave up after 5 yrs. Glasses and crystal comes out shiny, dishes without any residue even if I put them in without rinsing. It is a very quiet machine, and has a red light reflecting on the floor while working. I only had to lead the dishwasher salt once so far, it has been a month so still need to see how long would last. Overall Im very happy with the performance, the app features and ability to control remotely.

Loaded the dishwasher before bed, added the cascade packet (recommended by GE), set normal cycle and went to bed. Thr 11/6- washer reading “FTD” error code, the dishes unwashed and the tub of the washer full of dirty food water. Attempted to restart and the error code reappeared. 11/6- 1st call to Bodewell to see if the dishwasher was able to be fixed. CSR was dismissive and uninformative. She informed me that a technician would be at my house on F 11/21. I was confused as we had not discussed anything and I asked the CSR to give me a quote for this repair. She responded with “It's under warrantee… everyone knows that.” At no point had she discussed my warrantee nor the steps to proceed. I informed her that she had not communicated with me properly and she dismissed that concern as well. I confirmed (on a recorded line) that the technician would be at my home on 11/21 and that the repairs were 100% covered. She begrudgingly confirmed and we ended the call. On Thr 11/20, I received a call from Bodewell informing me that they were cancelling my Friday 11/21 appointment and rescheduling because I “did not have the necessary parts”. I was then informed that someone had gone in the system, ordered parts to be delivered to my house and that FEDEX had not reported movement on the shipment since 11/18, when they had been mis-shipped to Oregon. I had no idea about this part order, had no tracking information, and the initial CSR had not told me that the tech could not come out without parts. When I asked if anyone had spoken with FEDEX I was told that “was not their job” by Bodewell. I contacted FEDEX myself, filed a claim regarding the missing packages and gave them MY contact information. Bodewell refused to send the technician on 11/21 without those parts being present. I contacted FEDEX on 11/21 and they informed me that there was no movement on the packages and that they were not locatable. I called Bodewell back and informed them of this and the CSR “reordered” the parts to my house with overnight shipping. She then informed me that some of the parts were backordered but she would try to expedite them. My service appointment was rescheduled for Fri 11/28, the day AFTER thanksgiving between 8 and noon. On M 11/24, 3 packages from GE were on my doorstep. F 11/28, A Bodewell technician arrived within the time frame and got to work. GE had sent refrigerator parts to my home. Luckily the third package had a drain pump. The technician performed a general maintenance, changed the drain pump, ran a rinse cycle, deemed the dishwasher all set and left. Two hours later, I loaded the dishwasher, went to run a normal cycle and received FTD error code again. On Friday 11/28, called Bodewell at 4:30 pm to report dishwasher still broken. I was told that a technician would not be able to come out until Fri 12/12- I refused this and asked to be escalated. A supervisor never came on the line, but told the CSR to schedule us with a third-party appliance technician. The CSR scheduled the technician to come out today, Tue 12/2 between 8 and noon. This morning 12/2 I had yet to receive a confirmation. At 11 am I called Bodewell and the CSR gave me the contact information for the appliance repair company. This company is located in BROOKLYN, NY. A TWO HOUR DRIVE from my house. I call the appliance company- they had not received the claim from Bodewell until 9 am this morning 12/2, and could not (understandably) get a technician out to my location today. She asked if she could schedule me for the soonest I was available, which is Thursday 12/4, during the morning. I called Bodewell back to inquire why the CSR that made the appointment on Friday 11/28 had not confirmed with appointment with the company. The CSR's that I spoke to explained that their system does not always send the claim immediately. I explained to the CSR that this was unacceptable, I now had to wait until Thursday, and I asked if on Thursday, if the technician determined that the dishwasher was broken, would they be able to replace the unit. The CSR explained to me that this Thursday would be a diagnostic appointment. And that she was unable to send parts to my home in order to prepare for this maintenance. I asked to be transferred to customer relations. Once on the phone with customer relations, it took 56 minutes for someone to allow me to speak with a supervisor. I spent the entire time attempting to explain that if the procedures had been followed properly, I would already have had a repaired dishwasher, or a replacement on the way. The CSR at customer relations repeated the same line of 'this is how the warranty works' over and over. It seems to me that after one technician had already been out, there should have been some sort of reconciliation made. I asked that this CSR's contact the appliance company in Brooklyn, and ask which parts they thought may be needed to make the repairs on Thursday. At first she refused to make the call, but then she called the company repeatedly and they did not answer. She then informed me that they would not be ordering parts and should not order parts prior to a technician diagnosing the unit. I pointed out that GE had previously ordered parts to my home twice. I finally informed her that I would not be getting off the phone until I spoke with a supervisor. Once I was finally on the phone with a supervisor, the supervisor informed me with 0 hesitation that there was nothing that they would be doing for me that I had to wait for Thursday's appointment- at which point the dishwasher will be diagnosed. On Thursday, Bodewell will once again order parts, I will then have to wait for those parts to come in, and then wait for another appointment for another technician to come and install those parts. If those parts fail, I am still not eligible for a replacement. The supervisor informed me that GE requires the repair of a dishwasher to fail four times before they will issue a replacement. The supervisor noted that I had been lied to multiple times- starting with the fact that I had been informed that a technician could not come to my house without parts already on site. Two separate CSR's had informed me that my maintenance could not happen without those preordered parts. The supervisor seemed to think that I had originally had a technician out for a diagnostic appointment when I had never previously spoken to a technician before 11/28. The supervisor informed me that they are not allowed to order parts prior to a diagnostic appointment. This has occurred twice since my dishwasher broke. So- I am now set with a dilemma, I have a technician coming on Thursday who is unprepared (to no fault of their own) to fix my dishwasher. The GE/ Bodewell Warranty is nothing more than a con in order to make sales.It is costing both Bodewell and myself more money than it would cost for them to just replace the dishwasher. I will never buy another GE appliance again, and I encourage all my friends and family to follow suit. If you happen to have a GE appliance, pay close attention to the fact that your warranty does not actually cover the replacement of your appliance unless it has been repaired multiple times. You will wait months for these repairs, during which time your family will have to go through the same things that I go through. I am spending more time hand-washing dishes, and arguing with CSR's on the phone, than I am spending time with my family during the holiday season. I find GE, and their appliance repair company Bodewell, to be extremely negligent, rude, and ineffective.

Loaded the dishwasher before bed, added the cascade packet (recommended by GE), set normal cycle and went to bed. Thr 11/6- washer reading “FTD” error code, the dishes unwashed and the tub of the washer full of dirty food water. Attempted to restart and the error code reappeared. 11/6- 1st call to Bodewell to see if the dishwasher was able to be fixed. CSR was dismissive and uninformative. She informed me that a technician would be at my house on F 11/21. I was confused as we had not discussed anything and I asked the CSR to give me a quote for this repair. She responded with “It's under warrantee… everyone knows that.” At no point had she discussed my warrantee nor the steps to proceed. I informed her that she had not communicated with me properly and she dismissed that concern as well. I confirmed (on a recorded line) that the technician would be at my home on 11/21 and that the repairs were 100% covered. She begrudgingly confirmed and we ended the call. On Thr 11/20, I received a call from Bodewell informing me that they were cancelling my Friday 11/21 appointment and rescheduling because I “did not have the necessary parts”. I was then informed that someone had gone in the system, ordered parts to be delivered to my house and that FEDEX had not reported movement on the shipment since 11/18, when they had been mis-shipped to Oregon. I had no idea about this part order, had no tracking information, and the initial CSR had not told me that the tech could not come out without parts. When I asked if anyone had spoken with FEDEX I was told that “was not their job” by Bodewell. I contacted FEDEX myself, filed a claim regarding the missing packages and gave them MY contact information. Bodewell refused to send the technician on 11/21 without those parts being present. I contacted FEDEX on 11/21 and they informed me that there was no movement on the packages and that they were not locatable. I called Bodewell back and informed them of this and the CSR “reordered” the parts to my house with overnight shipping. She then informed me that some of the parts were backordered but she would try to expedite them. My service appointment was rescheduled for Fri 11/28, the day AFTER thanksgiving between 8 and noon. On M 11/24, 3 packages from GE were on my doorstep. F 11/28, A Bodewell technician arrived within the time frame and got to work. GE had sent refrigerator parts to my home. Luckily the third package had a drain pump. The technician performed a general maintenance, changed the drain pump, ran a rinse cycle, deemed the dishwasher all set and left. Two hours later, I loaded the dishwasher, went to run a normal cycle and received FTD error code again. On Friday 11/28, called Bodewell at 4:30 pm to report dishwasher still broken. I was told that a technician would not be able to come out until Fri 12/12- I refused this and asked to be escalated. A supervisor never came on the line, but told the CSR to schedule us with a third-party appliance technician. The CSR scheduled the technician to come out today, Tue 12/2 between 8 and noon. This morning 12/2 I had yet to receive a confirmation. At 11 am I called Bodewell and the CSR gave me the contact information for the appliance repair company. This company is located in BROOKLYN, NY. A TWO HOUR DRIVE from my house. I call the appliance company- they had not received the claim from Bodewell until 9 am this morning 12/2, and could not (understandably) get a technician out to my location today. She asked if she could schedule me for the soonest I was available, which is Thursday 12/4, during the morning. I called Bodewell back to inquire why the CSR that made the appointment on Friday 11/28 had not confirmed with appointment with the company. The CSR's that I spoke to explained that their system does not always send the claim immediately. I explained to the CSR that this was unacceptable, I now had to wait until Thursday, and I asked if on Thursday, if the technician determined that the dishwasher was broken, would they be able to replace the unit. The CSR explained to me that this Thursday would be a diagnostic appointment. And that she was unable to send parts to my home in order to prepare for this maintenance. I asked to be transferred to customer relations. Once on the phone with customer relations, it took 56 minutes for someone to allow me to speak with a supervisor. I spent the entire time attempting to explain that if the procedures had been followed properly, I would already have had a repaired dishwasher, or a replacement on the way. The CSR at customer relations repeated the same line of 'this is how the warranty works' over and over. It seems to me that after one technician had already been out, there should have been some sort of reconciliation made. I asked that this CSR's contact the appliance company in Brooklyn, and ask which parts they thought may be needed to make the repairs on Thursday. At first she refused to make the call, but then she called the company repeatedly and they did not answer. She then informed me that they would not be ordering parts and should not order parts prior to a technician diagnosing the unit. I pointed out that GE had previously ordered parts to my home twice. I finally informed her that I would not be getting off the phone until I spoke with a supervisor. Once I was finally on the phone with a supervisor, the supervisor informed me with 0 hesitation that there was nothing that they would be doing for me that I had to wait for Thursday's appointment- at which point the dishwasher will be diagnosed. On Thursday, Bodewell will once again order parts, I will then have to wait for those parts to come in, and then wait for another appointment for another technician to come and install those parts. If those parts fail, I am still not eligible for a replacement. The supervisor informed me that GE requires the repair of a dishwasher to fail four times before they will issue a replacement. The supervisor noted that I had been lied to multiple times- starting with the fact that I had been informed that a technician could not come to my house without parts already on site. Two separate CSR's had informed me that my maintenance could not happen without those preordered parts. The supervisor seemed to think that I had originally had a technician out for a diagnostic appointment when I had never previously spoken to a technician before 11/28. The supervisor informed me that they are not allowed to order parts prior to a diagnostic appointment. This has occurred twice since my dishwasher broke. So- I am now set with a dilemma, I have a technician coming on Thursday who is unprepared (to no fault of their own) to fix my dishwasher. The GE/ Bodewell Warranty is nothing more than a con in order to make sales.It is costing both Bodewell and myself more money than it would cost for them to just replace the dishwasher. I will never buy another GE appliance again, and I encourage all my friends and family to follow suit. If you happen to have a GE appliance, pay close attention to the fact that your warranty does not actually cover the replacement of your appliance unless it has been repaired multiple times. You will wait months for these repairs, during which time your family will have to go through the same things that I go through. I am spending more time hand-washing dishes, and arguing with CSR's on the phone, than I am spending time with my family during the holiday season. I find GE, and their appliance repair company Bodewell, to be extremely negligent, rude, and ineffective.

I confirmed (on a recorded line) that the technician would be at my home on 11/21 and that the repairs were 100% covered. I had no idea about this part order, had no tracking information, and the initial CSR had not told me that the tech could not come out without parts. When I asked if anyone had spoken with FEDEX I was told that “was not their job” by Bodewell. I contacted FEDEX myself, filed a claim regarding the missing packages and gave them MY contact information. Bodewell refused to send the technician on 11/21 without those parts being present. I contacted FEDEX on 11/21 and they informed me that there was no movement on the packages and that they were not locatable. I called Bodewell back and informed them of this and the CSR “reordered” the parts to my house with overnight shipping. She then informed me that some of the parts were backordered but she would try to expedite them. My service appointment was rescheduled for Fri 11/28, the day AFTER thanksgiving between 8 and noon.On M 11/24, 3 packages from GE were on my doorstep.F 11/28, A Bodewell technician arrived within the time frame and got to work. The technician performed a general maintenance, changed the drain pump, ran a rinse cycle, deemed the dishwasher all set and left.Two hours later, I loaded the dishwasher, went to run a normal cycle and received FTD error code again. On Friday 11/28, called Bodewell at 4:30 pm to report dishwasher still broken. I was told that a technician would not be able to come out until Fri 12/12- I refused this and asked to be escalated. A supervisor never came on the line, but told the CSR to schedule us with a third-party appliance technician. The CSR scheduled the technician to come out today, Tue 12/2 between 8 and noon.This morning 12/2 I had yet to receive a confirmation. At 11 am I called Bodewell and the CSR gave me the contact information for the appliance repair company. This company is located in BROOKLYN, NY. A TWO HOUR DRIVE from my house. I call the appliance company- they had not received the claim from Bodewell until 9 am this morning 12/2, and could not (understandably) get a technician out to my location today. She asked if she could schedule me for the soonest I was available, which is Thursday 12/4, during the morning.I called Bodewell back to inquire why the CSR that made the appointment on Friday 11/28 had not confirmed with appointment with the company. The CSR's that I spoke to explained that their system does not always send the claim immediately. I explained to the CSR that this was unacceptable, I now had to wait until Thursday, and I asked if on Thursday, if the technician determined that the dishwasher was broken, would they be able to replace the unit. The CSR explained to me that this Thursday would be a diagnostic appointment. And that she was unable to send parts to my home in order to prepare for this maintenance. I asked to be transferred to customer relations.Once on the phone with customer relations, it took 56 minutes for someone to allow me to speak with a supervisor. I spent the entire time attempting to explain that if the procedures had been followed properly, I would already have had a repaired dishwasher, or a replacement on the way. The CSR at customer relations repeated the same line of ‘this is how the warranty works’ over and over. I asked that this CSR's contact the appliance company in Brooklyn, and ask which parts they thought may be needed to make the repairs on Thursday. She then informed me that they would not be ordering parts and should not order parts prior to a technician diagnosing the unit. I pointed out that GE had previously ordered parts to my home twice. I finally informed her that I would not be getting off the phone until I spoke with a supervisor.Once I was finally on the phone with a supervisor, the supervisor informed me with 0 hesitation that there was nothing that they would be doing for me that I had to wait for Thursday's appointment- at which point the dishwasher will be diagnosed. If those parts fail, I am still not eligible for a replacement. The supervisor informed me that GE requires the repair of a dishwasher to fail four times before they will issue a replacement.The supervisor noted that I had been lied to multiple times- starting with the fact that I had been informed that a technician could not come to my house without parts already on site. Two separate CSR's had informed me that my maintenance could not happen without those preordered parts. The supervisor seemed to think that I had originally had a technician out for a diagnostic appointment when I had never previously spoken to a technician before 11/28. The supervisor informed me that they are not allowed to order parts prior to a diagnostic appointment. This has occurred twice since my dishwasher broke.So- I am now set with a dilemma, I have a technician coming on Thursday who is unprepared (to no fault of their own) to fix my dishwasher. Loaded the dishwasher before bed, added the cascade packet (recommended by GE), set normal cycle and went to bed. Thr 11/6- washer reading “FTD” error code, the dishes unwashed and the tub of the washer full of dirty food water. Attempted to restart and the error code reappeared. 11/6- 1st call to Bodewell to see if the dishwasher was able to be fixed. CSR was dismissive and uninformative. She informed me that a technician would be at my house on F 11/21. I was confused as we had not discussed anything and I asked the CSR to give me a quote for this repair. She responded with “It's under warrantee… everyone knows that.” At no point had she discussed my warrantee nor the steps to proceed. I informed her that she had not communicated with me properly and she dismissed that concern as well. I confirmed (on a recorded line) that the technician would be at my home on 11/21 and that the repairs were 100% covered. She begrudgingly confirmed and we ended the call. On Thr 11/20, I received a call from Bodewell informing me that they were cancelling my Friday 11/21 appointment and rescheduling because I “did not have the necessary parts”. I was then informed that someone had gone in the system, ordered parts to be delivered to my house and that FEDEX had not reported movement on the shipment since 11/18, when they had been mis-shipped to Oregon. I had no idea about this part order, had no tracking information, and the initial CSR had not told me that the tech could not come out without parts. When I asked if anyone had spoken with FEDEX I was told that “was not their job” by Bodewell. I contacted FEDEX myself, filed a claim regarding the missing packages and gave them MY contact information. Bodewell refused to send the technician on 11/21 without those parts being present. I contacted FEDEX on 11/21 and they informed me that there was no movement on the packages and that they were not locatable. I called Bodewell back and informed them of this and the CSR “reordered” the parts to my house with overnight shipping. She then informed me that some of the parts were backordered but she would try to expedite them. My service appointment was rescheduled for Fri 11/28, the day AFTER thanksgiving between 8 and noon. On M 11/24, 3 packages from GE were on my doorstep. F 11/28, A Bodewell technician arrived within the time frame and got to work. GE had sent refrigerator parts to my home. Luckily the third package had a drain pump. The technician performed a general maintenance, changed the drain pump, ran a rinse cycle, deemed the dishwasher all set and left. Two hours later, I loaded the dishwasher, went to run a normal cycle and received FTD error code again. On Friday 11/28, called Bodewell at 4:30 pm to report dishwasher still broken. I was told that a technician would not be able to come out until Fri 12/12- I refused this and asked to be escalated. A supervisor never came on the line, but told the CSR to schedule us with a third-party appliance technician. The CSR scheduled the technician to come out today, Tue 12/2 between 8 and noon. This morning 12/2 I had yet to receive a confirmation. At 11 am I called Bodewell and the CSR gave me the contact information for the appliance repair company. This company is located in BROOKLYN, NY. A TWO HOUR DRIVE from my house. I call the appliance company- they had not received the claim from Bodewell until 9 am this morning 12/2, and could not (understandably) get a technician out to my location today. She asked if she could schedule me for the soonest I was available, which is Thursday 12/4, during the morning. I called Bodewell back to inquire why the CSR that made the appointment on Friday 11/28 had not confirmed with appointment with the company. The CSR's that I spoke to explained that their system does not always send the claim immediately. I explained to the CSR that this was unacceptable, I now had to wait until Thursday, and I asked if on Thursday, if the technician determined that the dishwasher was broken, would they be able to replace the unit. The CSR explained to me that this Thursday would be a diagnostic appointment. And that she was unable to send parts to my home in order to prepare for this maintenance. I asked to be transferred to customer relations. Once on the phone with customer relations, it took 56 minutes for someone to allow me to speak with a supervisor. I spent the entire time attempting to explain that if the procedures had been followed properly, I would already have had a repaired dishwasher, or a replacement on the way. The CSR at customer relations repeated the same line of 'this is how the warranty works' over and over. It seems to me that after one technician had already been out, there should have been some sort of reconciliation made. I asked that this CSR's contact the appliance company in Brooklyn, and ask which parts they thought may be needed to make the repairs on Thursday. At first she refused to make the call, but then she called the company repeatedly and they did not answer. She then informed me that they would not be ordering parts and should not order parts prior to a technician diagnosing the unit. I pointed out that GE had previously ordered parts to my home twice. I finally informed her that I would not be getting off the phone until I spoke with a supervisor. Once I was finally on the phone with a supervisor, the supervisor informed me with 0 hesitation that there was nothing that they would be doing for me that I had to wait for Thursday's appointment- at which point the dishwasher will be diagnosed. On Thursday, Bodewell will once again order parts, I will then have to wait for those parts to come in, and then wait for another appointment for another technician to come and install those parts. If those parts fail, I am still not eligible for a replacement. The supervisor informed me that GE requires the repair of a dishwasher to fail four times before they will issue a replacement. The supervisor noted that I had been lied to multiple times- starting with the fact that I had been informed that a technician could not come to my house without parts already on site. Two separate CSR's had informed me that my maintenance could not happen without those preordered parts. The supervisor seemed to think that I had originally had a technician out for a diagnostic appointment when I had never previously spoken to a technician before 11/28. The supervisor informed me that they are not allowed to order parts prior to a diagnostic appointment. This has occurred twice since my dishwasher broke. So- I am now set with a dilemma, I have a technician coming on Thursday who is unprepared (to no fault of their own) to fix my dishwasher. The GE/ Bodewell Warranty is nothing more than a con in order to make sales.It is costing both Bodewell and myself more money than it would cost for them to just replace the dishwasher. I will never buy another GE appliance again, and I encourage all my friends and family to follow suit. If you happen to have a GE appliance, pay close attention to the fact that your warranty does not actually cover the replacement of your appliance unless it has been repaired multiple times. You will wait months for these repairs, during which time your family will have to go through the same things that I go through. I am spending more time hand-washing dishes, and arguing with CSR's on the phone, than I am spending time with my family during the holiday season. I find GE, and their appliance repair company Bodewell, to be extremely negligent, rude, and ineffective.

Sentence (English): When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

LG 브랜드의 안정성, 세척력, 소음, 전력 효율까지 고려하면 이 가격대에서는 충분히 경쟁력 있는 모델이라고 생각합니다.전체적으로 매우 만족하지만, 설치 경험에서 경도 설정 안내가 부족했던 점만은 아쉽습니다. 그 부분만 제외하면 성능, 용량, 사용 편의성 모두 기대 이상이었습니다.결론적으로 열풍건조나 자동문 열림 같은 고급 기능보다 기본 세척력, 가성비, 브랜드 안정성을 우선으로 보는 분들께 추천할 만한 모델입니다. 경도 설정만 제대로 해두면 물자국과 냄새 없이 깔끔하게 마무리되므로 실사용 중심의 가정이라면 충분히 만족하실 거라 생각합니다.

These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Sentence (English): Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Sentence (English): This was disappointing.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Sentence (English): Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Sentence (English): It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Sentence (English): I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

Sentence (English): Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model.
Comments (English): [ If you look at basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and stability, this is it. ] || ---------------- || When choosing appliances, I prefer reliable basic performance over unnecessary features. Dishwashers were no exception. These days, there are many extra features like hot air drying and automatic door opening, but ultimately, I believe appliances are consumables that break down over time, so I decided that a balance between price and core features was more important. Based on these criteria, I chose the LG DUE1BGLE dishwasher. Having previously used a six-person dishwasher, I was definitely satisfied with its cleaning performance. However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. However, after adjusting the water hardness with salt and water, the cleaning power and rinsing results were completely different. Water stains were nearly gone, and the smell was gone, so I was completely satisfied with the basic cleaning performance of this model. The internal structure has two upper and lower compartments, and it can easily handle a day's worth of dishes for a family of three who uses a lot of dishes. It can handle bulky kitchen items like pots, frying pans, and cutting boards all at once, significantly reducing the stress of dishwashing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. Unlike a washing machine, it doesn't vibrate or move around much, which is another plus, making it less sensitive to installation conditions. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Aside from that, the performance, capacity, and ease of use all exceeded my expectations. In conclusion, this model is recommended for those who prioritize basic cleaning power, cost-effectiveness, and brand reliability over advanced features like hot air drying and automatic door opening. With the right hardness setting, it will cleanly finish without water marks or odors, so I think it will be sufficiently satisfying for households focused on practical use.

However, at first, I noticed some water stains on the cups and spoons, and a fishy smell after rinsing, so I thought it was a product issue. It turned out that the water hardness setting was set to the default, and the installer hadn't explained the water hardness or how to adjust it from the beginning. This was disappointing. The drying function might be disappointing for those who absolutely need hot air drying. However, since I don't place a high value on the drying function, I find this model quite reasonable. While it uses internal temperature and residual heat to dry, if you adjust the firmness setting precisely, there are virtually no water marks after drying, so I didn't experience any inconvenience in actual use. The noise level is also acceptable. Even when running it in the evening, it wasn't too bothersome, and the only noise you'll hear is a slight rattling of the dishes during operation. I wasn't expecting this product to be flashy, but rather a reliable performer for the price, and it exceeded my expectations. Considering the LG brand's reliability, cleaning power, noise reduction, and power efficiency, I think this model is a competitively priced model. Overall, I'm very satisfied, but my only regret was the lack of guidance on setting the firmness during installation. Sentence (English): In general, Bosch dishwashers are great and I wouldn't own any other brand (this is my second one).
Comments (English): In general, Bosch dishwashers are great and I wouldn't own any other brand (this is my second one). With that being said though, this one isn't as impressive as my old Bosch. It's only two DB louder, so that is barely noticeable. What I really miss is my large cutlery holder in my old one. This one comes with a tiny cutlery holder, which doesn't work for my family. I actually kept my old one and have placed it in this new DW. The other items I miss were the controls on the top and the light that would show it was running on the floor. There is really no way to tell this one is running unless you listen for it. I could also leave my old DW "on" (lights on top working) until we emptied it, which let everyone know that those were clean dishes in there. These are all minimal things, so I still love my dishwasher. I'm really just hoping Bosch takes notice of these issues to make the next models better. I still wouldn't own any other model and I do love the fingerprint resistant stainless finish on this DW. We also got this for a fantastic price that I couldn't find from any other store.

Sentence (English): I previoulsy owned an earlier model of this GE dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Functionally questionable. ] || ---------------- || I previoulsy owned an earlier model of this GE dishwasher. So, I thought this would have been an upgrade as its slightly quiter and figured we could get allot of use out of the bottle cleaner being in the middle rack as to avoid warpage from the heat on the bottom rack. Giving this a 1 star as a steak knife fell out of the top drawer as I opened it. I did not jerk or quickly generate a rip open motion, just a simple slightly slower open (knowing the knife was there) and the knife was apparently close enough to the edge to fall through and boom, right there 3" away from my foot. The grating of the top drawer has been altered from our previous model where it used to be a rigid hard plastic with no open perimter edges that can easy contain chop sticks, to one now where the edges are open and everything falls through the edges, gets caught in the middle, everywhere. This design is pretty unfotunately as most handles will slip into the open grate area The other issue that I gambled on is the bottle cleaning feature. I guessed it may not serve larger bottles and unfortunately it does not. This concentrated blast feature in my previous model was located under the silverware section, where it is needed the most. Overall, it is quieter, it does clean well, and dries ~80%, but i need to hand drying before putting many items away including nearly everything on the top rack.

Sentence (English): LG Electronics Dios Objet Collection 12-seater built-in dishwasher.
Comments (English): LG Electronics Dios Objet Collection 12-seater built-in dishwasher. The motherboard of my previous built-in dishwasher died, so I had to purchase a new one. The LG Dios Objet Collection dishwasher was the first thing I was impressed with: its design blends seamlessly into the kitchen. Our kitchen sink is also beige, so I was worried the colors wouldn't match, but the Objet's unique, luxurious color scheme complements the overall look of the kitchen. And because it's built-in, it's also great for space utilization. We use powdered detergent, and the cleaning power exceeded my expectations. It even washes greasy frying pans and glasses cleanly without leaving any streaks. I especially love the auto-open feature. Since the interior is often humid, it automatically opens and closes after 2-3 hours, ensuring the dishwasher dries completely. It's also quieter than I expected, so I didn't find it annoying even at night. The internal layout, with its efficient placement of cutlery and small dishes, is also more convenient than my previous model. Overall, I'm satisfied with this product in terms of cleaning power, design, and ease of use. I'm also happy that I can apply for the Premium Efficiency rating! It was a satisfying purchase.

Sentence (English): My wife is pregnant and can't cook because of morning sickness.
Comments (English): My wife is pregnant and can't cook because of morning sickness. Cooking and washing dishes are such a struggle. I've been reminded of my mother's greatness every day. I remember using a built-in dishwasher at my parents' house 15 years ago, so I figured any LG model would be better than that. So, I bought the due4bge model on sale this time. I was debating whether to buy it or not, but I missed the 11th Street special price of 550,000 won, which was a shame. But the final purchase price, including credit card discounts and energy rebates, was 630,000 won, and I've finally freed myself from the hassle of washing dishes. Could there be a more satisfying appliance? It's a bit noisy, like a washing machine, but I'm extremely satisfied with the results. The only difference between the higher-end model and the due6bge is the lack of two features, and the price difference is about 400,000 won, even on special. I didn't think the hot air dryer was worth more than 400,000 won, so I chose the lower-end model. The offline model costs 160-170, so there's no comparison. And I also didn't want to bother with the spoon. I purchased this product because I thought it would be perfect for my needs. It also has an automatic door opening feature, so I think it's a revolutionary innovation. I plan to use it for a long time.

Sentence (English): I have no other experience with the dishwasher, but a nice bonus was that there were already detergents for the first wash inside.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher, washes dishes = main reason for purchase. ] || ---------------- || I have no other experience with the dishwasher, but a nice bonus was that there were already detergents for the first wash inside. I would appreciate if the package included at least a paper measuring tape for positioning the front panel of the built-in dishwasher (similar to what other brands do). Comments (Original): [ Fajn myčka, myje nádobí = hlavní důvod koupě. ] || ---------------- || Nemám jiné zkušenosti s myčkou, ale fajn bonus byl, že uvnitř byly už prostředky na první mytí. Takže funguje jak bych očekával, doufám, že bude fungovat dlouho. Ocenil bych kdyby součástí balení byl třeba alespoň papírový měřák na umístění čelní desky vestavné myčky (podobně jak to dělají jiné značky). Nebo možná tam byl a omylem jsem ho vyhodil, ale nemyslím si. Nicméně díky za myčku.

Comments (English): [ Great choice ] || ---------------- || #promotionmotivatedopinion I'd like to share my opinion on the Bosch SMV4ENX06E dishwasher. This is a fully built-in model from the Serie 4 series, which I chose for my kitchen, looking for an appliance that would be efficient and, most importantly for me, very quiet. My brief impressions of the SMV4ENX06E dishwasher: I'm really pleased with this dishwasher. From the very first time I used it, I was especially surprised by its quiet operation. The claimed 42 dB in practice means that in an open-plan kitchen and living room, it's almost inaudible, and the special "Quiet" program, operating at 41 dB, is a real hit when I turn it on late in the evening. As for its efficiency, I have no complaints. Dishes, even those with dried-on dinner leftovers, always come out clean. I highly appreciate the EfficientDry drying system. At the end of the program, the dishwasher door opens automatically, which significantly improves drying results, especially for plastic containers, and I don't have to worry about steam building up inside. In terms of loading, the third ExtraSpace cutlery rack is a huge advantage for me. This solution frees up space in the lower rack, allowing me to fit larger pots and pans. Loading flexibility is excellent, and the adjustable racks allow me to adapt the interior to different dishware shapes. I also use the Home Connect app. It's convenient that I can remotely start the wash when I'm away or check how much time is left until the end of the cycle. A red beam of light projected onto the floor indicates the wash cycle in progress. When the program ends, the light automatically turns off, so you don't have to open the door to check the status, although it actually opens automatically to dry dishes. In my opinion, this dishwasher is worth recommending. It combines high-quality washing and drying with modern conveniences and the comfort of quiet operation.

Comments (English): [ Solid investment ] || ---------------- || I've been using this 24-inch stainless steel dishwasher for just over a year now, and overall, I'm really pleased with it. It has a sleek, modern look that complements my kitchen perfectly. The brushed stainless steel finish gives it a premium feel, and the pocket handle is a nice touch—it's subtle and blends seamlessly into the design. The unit feels sturdy and solid, which is something I've appreciated from the start.Performance:The AI intelligent wash system is a standout feature. It adjusts water pressure and cycle time based on the load, so I don't have to worry about choosing the right cycle each time. Dishes come out consistently clean. There's a noticeable difference in cleaning power compared to my old dishwasher. I rarely need to use the "heavy" cycle, as it handles everything well on the normal setting.Drying:The drying performance is a nice added feature, most of the dishes come out completely dry, which is a huge upgrade from my previous machine. I've noticed some minor scratches on the exterior from daily use, but that's to be expected with stainless steel.
